title: Chess, But My Pieces Have Gravity
summary: Real-time chess platformer: the board is seen side-on with gravity (rank 1 is the floor). The player directly controls only his king like a platformer character - run left/right, jump, stand on top of enemy pieces - and the king carries a (Minecraft diamond) sword: jumping/landing on an enemy piece stabs and removes it. Stockfish plays its full army on a timer, snapping the king to its nearest square and moving to capture it. Stabbing the enemy king wins; being captured loses. Narrator beats Stockfish at 1 move/3 s, 2 s, 1 s and finally 0.5 s, mostly by sniping rooks/queens and using pawn 'ladders' to climb to the black king.
rules: Board 8x8 viewed from the side with gravity; the player's king is a free-moving platformer avatar (no other white pieces mentioned/needed).
Controls: move left/right, jump (limited jump height - one rank-ish), stand on pieces; landing on/attacking an enemy piece with the sword removes it ('snipe').
Stockfish moves its pieces on a fixed timer: one move every 3 s (game 1), 2 s, 1 s, 0.5 s (final boss).
For Stockfish's move generation the king is rounded to its nearest square; if a black piece moves onto/captures that square the king is captured and the player loses.
Pawns cannot move backwards, so standing on pawns is relatively safe; pieces can capture backwards so standing on them is risky.
Stabbing the enemy king wins the game.
win_condition: Stab (land on) the black king before being captured; clear all four speed levels.
